solutions.solution: flap; f/l/short-a/p, spelling f-l-a-p then reread.

solutions.input: slam vowel to sit; then l to w
solutions.solution: slim, then swim; four phonemes each, one named substitution per step; retain s and m.

solutions.input: tail in dog wagged its tail, dictated
solutions.solution: tail; t/long-a/l, t-ai-l three phonemes, four letters. Context selects tail not tale; conventional word exact.

solutions.input: bright in lamp is bright, dictated
solutions.solution: bright; b/r/long-i/t four phonemes. Spell b-r-igh-t, six letters; retain final t and gh within vowel spelling.

solutions.input: sunhat in packed my sunhat, dictated
solutions.solution: sunhat = sun+hat. Six phonemes in common pronunciation; s-u-n-h-a-t six letters and two meaningful words.

solutions.input: some in There is some milk, dictated
solutions.solution: some; s/vowel-in-come/m, o encodes short-u here and final e not pronounced separately; s-o-m-e then reread. Giving come clue is support and must be recorded.

solutions.input: painted in Yesterday I painted a box, dictated
solutions.solution: painted = paint+ed; retain a-i and add e-d, past-time ending adds a syllable. Exact painted spelling and actual rereading required.

solutions.input: pack again from known base pack
solutions.solution: repack = re+pack; re before base means again. Example: I will repack my bag. Retain pack including ck.

solutions.input: someone who packs from base pack
solutions.solution: packer = pack+er; suffix er after pack names a person doing action. Retain pack and conventional spelling packer.

finding.location: AC9E2LY10 packet Map, write and reread/adult dictation card
finding.impact: Adult is told both to say the target and not pronounce the written answer before spelling. Literal directions conflict, creating avoidable ambiguity about necessary dictation.
finding.recommended: Say the target word and its sentence aloud. Keep the printed word hidden and do not name its letters or show its spelling until the learner has written it.
